✗ Service/payments is unhealthy

ROOT CAUSE
  Container "api" is failing its readiness probe (3 of 3 Pods)

  A container that fails its readiness probe is removed from the endpoints of
  every Service that selects this Pod, so it receives no traffic. Kubernetes
  reports that the probe failed; the reason the application answered that way is
  in its own logs.

  Evidence
    reason                 Unhealthy
      Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
    readinessProbe         http GET /healthz on port 8080
    readinessProbe.timing  delay 5s, period 10s, timeout 1s, failureThreshold 3

  Possible causes
    • the application is not listening on the probed port or path yet
    • the application takes longer to answer than the probe allows
    • the probe points at a port or path the application does not serve

  Suggested action
    Compare the probe's target with what the application actually serves, and
    check the container's logs around the failures.
      kubectl logs payments-abc -n prod -c api

CONSEQUENCE
  The Service has no ready endpoints, so it accepts no traffic

  Kubernetes only routes traffic to endpoints that report ready. A Pod is
  removed from a Service's endpoints while it fails its readiness probe, while
  it is starting, and while it is terminating.

  Evidence
    readyEndpoints     0
    matchingPods       3
    notReadyEndpoints  3

  Suggested action
    Look at the backend Pods: a Service with matching Pods and no ready
    endpoints is almost always a readiness problem in the Pods themselves.

Service
  Type        ClusterIP
  Cluster IP  10.96.0.10
  Selector    app=payments

Backends
  Matching Pods    3
  Ready endpoints  0 of 3  from EndpointSlice

Backend Pods
  payments-abc  NotReady  1h old
  payments-def  NotReady  1h old
  payments-ghi  NotReady  1h old

Ports
  80/TCP  targets 8080
